minutes.headline: Committee voted to send the FY25 warrant article to the town and heard ARPA studio equipment purchase plans.
minutes.summary: The Public Access Cable Committee approved prior minutes, heard the manager's monthly report (new programs, annual report draft, ARPA purchases for studio enhancements), and voted to submit the FY25 warrant article. The treasurer reported on the enterprise fund investment. A possible name/branding change was put on the next agenda. A motion to adjourn was made; the vote count was not fully captioned.

what_happened.line: The committee voted unanimously to send the FY25 warrant article for the public access enterprise operating and capital budgets to the town.
The manager reported plans to buy phase-one studio equipment with ARPA money, which requires a transfer to the B&O line; the lower of two quotes was noted.
The treasurer reported on the enterprise fund investment, including a year-end projection, and said two interest lines will appear in the budget.
A possible name or branding change was placed on the next meeting agenda, and the annual report was set to go in around mid-February.

why_it_matters: The warrant article is how the public access budget, which is funded through the cable enterprise fund and not the general tax levy, reaches the town's budget process and a later vote.
The ARPA purchases show how one-time federal pandemic money is being turned into studio equipment, with a transfer still needed to pay for phase one.
watch_next: Budget spreadsheets are due to the town by a mid-March date, and a draft is expected before the next committee meeting.
The next agenda is to carry the possible name or branding change.
